title: Affine section orbit criterion for arbitrary lines on smooth schemes over a normal affine base
statement: Let $A$ be a Noetherian normal domain [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-pbc-normal-ring] and put $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $H\to S$ be a smooth separated group scheme of finite type with geometrically connected fibres (for every field $\Omega$ and every morphism $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to S$ the fibre $H_\Omega=H\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ is connected) [def-pc-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-connected-scheme]. Here a group scheme has multiplication, identity and inverse satisfying the group identities; separated means that its diagonal is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Let $X\to S$ be smooth, separated and of finite type, with an action $a:H\times_SX\to X$ satisfying unit and associativity [def-pc-fibre-product]. Let $L$ be any invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-sc-invertible-module]. Form the open $V\subseteq X$ which is the union of all affine nonvanishing opens $X_s$, for all $n\geq1$ and all global sections $s\in\Gamma(X,L^{\otimes n})$, using [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]. If $a(H\times_SV)=X$ on underlying points, then $L$ is ample in the absolute sense. No square condition on $L$, generic-fibre connectedness of $X$, section of $X\to S$, transitivity, commutativity or properness is assumed. Empty $X$ is allowed.

source.place: Proposition 6.4(b), sufficient direction, printed p.15, smooth Noetherian specialization and affine rather than quasi-affine section loci. The proof includes reduction by normal components and fpqc descent, not a square-condition hypothesis. Online primary text read; local PDF WANTED.

proof.text: First work with any normal integral Noetherian affine base $S$. The original $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$ is such a base: [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs] gives quasi-compactness, and the one affine chart with Noetherian ring $A$ gives local Noetherianity. Its stalks are the prime localizations of $A$ by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization]. A monic equation for $z\in\operatorname{Frac}(A)$ over $A_{\mathfrak p}$ has a common denominator $t\notin\mathfrak p$; multiplying by $t^{\deg P}$ makes $tz$ integral over $A$, hence $tz\in A$ and $z\in A_{\mathfrak p}$. Thus those stalks are normal domains. A smooth finite-type $Y\to S$ is normal by [lem-sfb-smooth-normal-ascent] and Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. Smoothness gives local finite presentation by [lem-pc-smooth-flat]; finite type gives quasi-compactness, and separatedness gives quasi-separatedness. These are the finite-presentation hypotheses needed below.

source.place: Normality preparation: Stacks 034F; finite-type Noetherian ascent 01T6; affine stalks 01HV. Guo Proposition 6.4, first paragraph.

proof.text: Here is the elementary invariance observation used throughout. On a normal Noetherian $Y$, [rem-pc-regular-normal](2) gives finitely many disjoint integral clopen components. Label them by a finite discrete set. For any $y\in Y$, the orbit map $H_{\kappa(y)}\to Y$ lands in a single label: its source is connected by the geometric connectedness hypothesis, and the inverse images of labels form a finite disjoint clopen partition. The identity maps to $y$, so that label is the component of $y$. This proves that every component is stable under the action. The same argument works after any base change for which the target is normal Noetherian. Applying inversion also shows $a^{-1}(C)=H\times_SC$ for any such component $C$. The equality is scheme-theoretic because these are open subschemes. In particular, a surjective orbit map restricts to a surjective orbit map on each component.

source.place: Proposition 6.4, reduction to normal components; connected-to-discrete label argument written out.

proof.text: The orbit-cover hypothesis is preserved by affine base change and restriction to a clopen invariant component. Indeed, for affine $B\to S$, pull back each supplied section $s$ to $Y_B$. Its nonvanishing locus is $(Y_s)_B$: in the fibre it is $s(y)\otimes1$, nonzero exactly when $s(y)$ is, by [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor](3). If $Y_s$ is affine, this locus is affine by [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra]. Its intersection with a clopen component $C$ is affine by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-affine-cover-criterion](1). These intersections are exactly the loci of the restricted sections. The given surjection $H\times_SV\to Y$ remains surjective by [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change]. The inverse-image equality of Step 2 then restricts it to a surjection onto $C$. Thus the affine section loci for the restricted line meet every orbit. We need only these pulled-back sections, not an assertion that all sections descend.

source.place: Proposition 6.4, preservation of the hypothesis in component/base reductions; Stacks affine fibre product and closed affine criterion 01QO.

proof.text: Prove first the pointed case: $Y$ is integral, has an $S$-section, and $Y_\eta$ is geometrically integral. Apply [lem-sfb-pointed-generic-integral-action-square-power] to obtain $r\geq1$ such that $M=L^{\otimes r}$ satisfies the square condition. For every affine locus $Y_s$ with $s\in\Gamma(Y,L^{\otimes n})$, the section $s^{\otimes r}$ of $M^{\otimes n}$ has the same locus: in a local frame its coefficient is $f^r$, which is nonzero in a residue field exactly when $f$ is. Hence the affine loci of $M$ still meet all orbits. Apply [lem-sfb-square-action-affine-orbit-criterion], using the finite-presentation hypotheses from Step 1, to obtain ampleness of $M$. An affine locus of a section of $M^{\otimes k}$ is also the same affine locus of a section of $L^{\otimes rk}$, with $rk\geq1$. Quasi-compactness is unchanged, so [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module] gives ampleness of $L$.

source.place: Proposition 6.4, preliminary pointed geometrically integral generic-fibre case; Proposition 5.9(1), followed by Corollary 6.5.

proof.text: Now prove the result for integral $Y$ by strong induction on $N=\rho_{Y/S}(Y)$, the number of geometric irreducible components of its generic fibre. The induction assertion quantifies over every normal integral Noetherian affine base, every smooth separated finite-type integral $Y$ over it, every group and line in the statement, and the orbit-cover hypothesis. Finiteness and positivity of $N$ are part of [lem-sfb-smooth-self-product-component-rank]. Thus the $N=0$ assertion is vacuous; empty schemes are dealt with at the end. For $N\geq1$ assume the assertion for every smaller count, and form $W=Y\times_SY$ with projection $\pi$ to its first factor and pulled-back line $L_W=\operatorname{pr}_2^*L$. The same cited node gives $W=\coprod_{i=0}^m C_i$, with the diagonal in $C_0$, a section of $C_0\to Y$, and geometric generic counts $1$ for $C_0$ and strictly less than $N$ for all $C_i$, $i>0$. This use does not assume that $Y\to S$ is surjective.

source.place: Proposition 6.4, final paragraph; strong induction made explicit using Lemma 4.3 for the self-product.

proof.text: Let $H_Y$ act on $W$ through the second factor: $h\cdot(y,z)=(y,hz)$. Its identity, inverse and associative laws are the original action laws. The group $H_Y\to Y$ remains smooth by [lem-pc-proper-base-change](2), and separated of finite type by [lem-pod-separated-finite-type-base-change]. Its fibres are geometrically connected directly by the original field-extension quantifier. The normal Noetherian component decomposition of $W$ is supplied by Step 5, so Step 2 makes each $C_i$ invariant for this action. For any nonempty affine open $B\subset Y$, restrict to $W_B=B\times_SY$ and $C_{i,B}$. The component lemma says that each $C_{i,B}$ is nonempty normal integral, smooth separated of finite type over the normal integral Noetherian affine $B$, with the same generic component count; $C_{0,B}$ has the restricted diagonal section and geometrically integral generic fibre. Step 3 supplies its orbit-cover hypothesis.

source.place: Proposition 6.4, self-base-change over affine opens of Y; Stacks smooth and separated finite-type base change.

proof.text: For each nonempty affine open $B\subset Y$, apply Step 4 to $C_{0,B}\to B$ and $L_W|_{C_{0,B}}$: all its pointed-case hypotheses were verified in Step 6. For $i>0$, apply the strong induction hypothesis to $C_{i,B}\to B$, whose positive count is strictly smaller than $N$. This gives ampleness of the pulled-back line on every $C_{i,B}$. They are finitely many disjoint clopen pieces covering $W_B$. A section of a positive tensor power on one piece extends by zero to the other pieces, by the sheaf gluing axiom; its nonvanishing locus in $W_B$ is exactly the given affine locus in that piece. Their finite union is quasi-compact since each piece is quasi-compact. Thus [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module] gives ampleness of $L_W|_{W_B}$. Empty affine opens give the empty scheme, satisfying the same definition. Consequently $L_W$ is relatively ample for $\pi:W\to Y$, meaning ample over every affine open of $Y$.

source.place: Proposition 6.4, induction step and disjoint-component assembly; the two calls are to earlier proved cases, not to a node containing the desired conclusion.

proof.text: Put $U=f(Y)\subseteq S$, where $f:Y\to S$. By [lem-pc-smooth-flat] and [lem-weil-pbc-flat-lfp-open], this is open. It is quasi-compact as the continuous image of the quasi-compact $Y$; hence it is a quasi-compact open of an affine scheme. The induced map $Y\to U$ is smooth by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-restrict-open-subschemes](a) and is surjective by the definition of $U$. Choose a finite affine open covering $\{B_j\}$ of $Y$ by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-finite-affine-open-cover]. The family $\{B_j\to U\}$ is fpqc in [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering]: the maps are flat by smoothness, and for an affine open $T\subset U$ cover the opens $B_j\cap f^{-1}(T)$ by affine opens; their images are open and cover $T$, so quasi-compactness of $T$ gives the required finite subfamily. This construction handles a proper open image $U\ne S$.

source.place: Proposition 6.4, replacement of the base by the image and fpqc descent; definition of an fpqc covering, Stacks 01UA.

proof.text: The base change of $Y\to U$ along $B_j\to U$ is $Y\times_U B_j\simeq B_j\times_SY=W_{B_j}$ (with the factors interchanged). The equality of fibre products holds because $U\to S$ is an open immersion and both structure maps factor through it. The line is the pullback from the second $Y$ factor, exactly the line of Step 7. That step was proved for every affine open $B\subset Y$, so the same assertion on affine opens of $B_j$ says that the line is relatively ample over $B_j$. Apply the scheme case of [lem-sfb-space-relative-ampleness-fpqc-descent] to this fpqc covering and this supplied invertible module. It gives that $L$ is relatively ample for $Y\to U$. No descent of an arbitrarily chosen line or of an action is being asserted: the line and scheme were supplied from the start.

source.place: Proposition 6.4, last sentence; Stacks 0D3C (scheme case of 0D2P).

proof.text: Because $U$ is a quasi-compact open subscheme of affine $S$, it is quasi-affine. By [lem-sfb-quasiaffine-affine-basic-open-criterion], each point of $U$ has an affine principal neighborhood $U_b$ for some $b\in\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$. These functions, viewed as sections of the first power of $\mathcal O_U$, and quasi-compactness give ampleness of $\mathcal O_U$ by [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]. The map $Y\to U$ is quasi-compact: $Y$ and $U$ are Noetherian, so its inverse images of affine opens are quasi-compact; equivalently use [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](1). Now [lem-sfb-relative-ample-absolute-twist], with relatively ample $L$ and ample $M=\mathcal O_U$, gives an ample $L\otimes f^*\mathcal O_U^{\otimes a}$ for some $a\geq0$. The canonical unit identifications turn this into $L$, so [lem-sc-ample-iso] gives absolute ampleness of $L$. This completes the induction, including $N=1$, where there are no components of smaller positive count.

source.place: Agent expansion of Guo Proposition 6.4 after replacing the affine base by its open image; Stacks 01QE and 0892.

proof.text: Return to arbitrary $X$ in the statement. Step 1 makes $X$ normal Noetherian; [rem-pc-regular-normal](2) gives a finite disjoint decomposition into nonempty normal integral clopen $X_j$. Each restriction $X_j\to S$ is smooth by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-restrict-open-subschemes] and separated of finite type: its diagonal is the pullback of the closed diagonal of $X$, and local finite type is local on the source and hence restricts to this open subscheme; quasi-compactness follows from its Noetherian source. Step 2 gives invariance, and restriction of each original section to $X_j$ gives an affine locus by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-affine-cover-criterion](1); the orbit cover restricts as in Step 2. The integral assertion just proved therefore makes $L|_{X_j}$ ample. Extend its witnessing sections by zero on the other clopen pieces, exactly as in Step 7. Quasi-compactness and the affine loci in [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module] prove that $L$ is ample on $X$. If $X$ is empty, quasi-compactness holds and the pointwise condition is vacuous, so the conclusion holds without an induction parameter.

source.place: Proposition 6.4, first paragraph and componentwise conclusion; empty-scheme case explicitly checked.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q15-7e515371c (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read in full: the item (statement unchanged, 11 steps), both new nodes, and every cited node's statement. The local Guo PDF is absent and the review service blocks network access, so I could not open Prop 6.4(b), Prop 5.9 or Lemma 4.3. Every step was checked on its own mathematics, and the proof is correctly marked agent-written. Steps: (1) the normality-of-localizations argument and the finite-presentation hypotheses are sound. (2) Clopen components are invariant because the residue-field orbit maps have connected sources, which gives a^{-1}(C)=H×C. (3) Affine loci survive base change and restriction to a component: affine fibre product, then closed-immersion preimage. (4) The pointed case meets all hypotheses of square-action-affine-orbit-criterion (affine base, finite presentation, connected fibres, square condition), and L^r ample implies L ample. (5-7) The strong induction on the geometric generic component count is set up over all normal Noetherian affine bases. C_0 is handled by the pointed case, the components with i>0 have count below N, N=1 gives W=C_0, and there is no circularity. (8) The open image U is handled with a correct fpqc subcover argument and is not assumed equal to S. (9) Y×_U B_j = B_j×_S Y and the scheme case of descent apply. (10) U quasi-affine makes O_U ample, and the twist lemma with ample-iso gives L ample. (11) Clopen assembly and the empty case are fine. New nodes: the self-product component node checks out (smooth hence open, so each C_i dominates; the counts sum to N; the diagonal's rational point makes the C_0 generic fibre geometrically integral, so the counts for i>0 are below N; affine restrictions keep the generic point). The pointed square-power node fits the theorem-of-the-square-up-to-a-power line (Raynaud, Faisceaux amples), has r chosen before B,g,h, and its trivial-action and Poincaré-bundle edge cases are consistent. Neither duplicates normal-group-square-power, dedekind-action-square-power, field-square-after-finite-extension, rem-pc-regular-normal or galois-splitting, and neither restates the item. Both are statement-only, with logged searches and correct created/blueprint fields.
